dct_description_sm: The Teshekpuk Herd was first identified as a distinct herd in 1978, based on a calving distribution that was geographically separate from the adjacent Western Arctic and Central Arctic herds (Davis and Valkenburg 1978).  Visual counts between 1978 and 1982 indicated approximately 4,000 caribou used the area near Teshekpuk Lakeduring the insect relief period (Davis et al. 1979, Reynolds 1981, Silva et al. 1985).  In 1984, the population was estimated using post -calving aggregation photography (Davis et al. 1979), and indicated a minimum population of 11,822 in 1984 (Carroll 1992). Growth continued through 2002, when the Teshekpuk Herd was estimated at a minimum of 45,122  individuals (Carroll 2003).  The growth rate between 1984 and 2002 was 7.4%  A post-calving photocensus was conducted in 2008; the estimate from this photocensus is  64,107, a growth rate of 5.9% between 2002 and 2008 (Parrett 2009).  Demographic indices collected since 1990 indicate that recruitment and mortality appear to be converging.
dct_title_s: Teshekpuk Caribou Herd Monitoring in Alaska
